headline: California's Great Shouting Evacuation Rated 1.5 Stars by Consumer Reports
deck: Officials tout inefficiencies as charming amenities in latest hospitality review.
article:
In an eye-opening report released yesterday, Consumer Reports has awarded California's Great Shouting Evacuation a dismal 1.5 stars. The review cites critical issues stemming from the recent mass misdirection that left 180,000 evacuees wandering helplessly around county fairgrounds, desperately seeking audible guidance from officials who were busy refining their vocal projection techniques.

A damning two-star deduction specifically targeted the contradictory shout vectors, which were noted to have caused significant confusion among displaced families. 'One minute, we were supposed to head east, then suddenly we were told to go back west toward the cotton candy stand,' commented local resident Mabel Thistlebloom, who reportedly lost her prized collection of maple syrup jugs in the process. 'I could hardly hear myself think, let alone understand the shouts.'

The newly minted Compliance Investigator, Hector Yellman, proudly logged 47 telegrams per hour defending his promotion quota, all while maintaining an impeccable shout score that he plans to showcase at the upcoming Bureaucrats’ Annual Gala. 'Who needs efficient evacuation when you have robust shouting efforts?' Yellman declared in a telegram addressed to concerned citizens, though it remains unclear if anyone managed to hear it over the din of chaos.

In a final note of bemusement, the report awarded a paltry half-star for rooftop semaphore visibility during peak commute hours, as well as the innovative use of hand signals to enhance guest engagement. Californians may not know where they're going, but at least they know how to get there—with enthusiasm.
author: Ernest W. Bluster, Senior Correspondent

oped.title: Shouting Evacuations: The Only Honest Way to Leave a Burning Building
oped.author: Sir Archibald Yellsworth III, Grand Chancellor of the Academy for Unnecessary Volume
oped.body: Consumer Reports can keep its 1.5 stars. The Great Shouting Evacuation succeeded precisely because it rejected efficiency for character. In a world of timid telegrams and wheedling bike messengers, only sustained bellowing ensures everyone hears the news before the flames arrive. The real failure lies with evacuees who insisted on wearing wide-brimmed hats that muffled incoming warnings. My own neighbor’s ridiculous fedora blocked three critical phrases about the south exit. Rather than coddle such vanity, we should mandate ear-trumpets and require daily vocal drills. Those who still cannot project deserve to learn the hard way. The system works; the people are simply too quiet. If anything, next year’s drills should begin at 6 a.m. sharp so the rest of us can finish our important morning shouting without interruptions from lesser voices.

Lost: one perfectly good evacuation route and my last shred of dignity, both scattered during yesterday's Great Shouting; reward is a strongly worded messenger note if returned promptly.

For sale: slightly battered bullhorns and three dozen bicycles from the failed shouting exodus, all rated charming by officials but useless for actual escape. Cash or telegram offers only, must collect before next review.
Public apology from the State Hospitality Board: our 1.5-star shouting evacuation was meant to feel quaint, not catastrophic; complimentary bike-messenger refunds available if you can still hear us.

stories.headline: Evacuated Residents Form Rooftop Shouting Committees Across Nevada Borders
stories.deck: HOA boards now require three-day telegram notice for any voice projection exceeding two blocks.
stories.article:
The 180,000 residents displaced by the shouting alerts have settled into host communities where daily updates travel via synchronized yells from strip-mall rooftops. Committees in Henderson and Mesquite coordinate lost-pet announcements and telegram forwarding schedules each dawn.

Local bylaws now mandate that all complaints about volume be delivered by bicycle messenger in triplicate, extending resolution times to nine business days. One Nevada subdivision reported its first successful reunion of siblings after a three-hour chain of echoed queries reached the correct cul-de-sac.

stories.headline: Telegram Firms Report Record Backlogs After Shouting-Based Order Systems Fail
stories.deck: Executives cite the absence of confirmation shouts as the primary cause of duplicated supply shipments.
stories.article:
Major retailers have abandoned shouted warehouse directives after repeated shipments of office chairs reached the wrong distribution centers in three states. Companies now require all purchase orders to travel by telegram, adding four to seven days to standard fulfillment cycles.

A Sacramento logistics provider introduced a new tier of "priority bicycle confirmation" at an extra fee, yet most clients still receive duplicate invoices because messengers cannot verify verbal corrections. Industry analysts project a 22 percent increase in physical paperwork storage costs by year end.

stories.headline: Bicycle Messenger Gangs Target Unverified Telegram Drop Boxes in Oakland
stories.deck: Police attribute the rise in thefts to the lack of immediate verbal confirmation at pickup points.
stories.article:
A coordinated ring of couriers has begun intercepting unsecured telegram bundles left at unmanned counters while recipients wait for shouted follow-up instructions that never arrive. Losses include payroll ledgers and court summonses across three counties.

Detectives note that the absence of telephones prevents rapid alerts to neighboring precincts, forcing officers to dispatch bicycle patrols with physical descriptions. One suspect was apprehended only after a six-hour relay of handwritten wanted notices reached the correct substation.
